stemBlocks.value: The functions f, g and h are defined by f: x ↦ x − 3, g: x ↦ x² and h: x ↦ x² − 6x + 9. (a) Given that f²(x) = f[f(x)], f³(x) = f[f²(x)] and so on, (i) deduce an algebraic expression in terms of x for f⁴(x) and hence calculate f⁴(3); (ii) show that gf(x) = h(x). (b)(i) Determine the values of x for which h(x) > 1. (b)(ii) Show that if h(x) < 25, then -2 < x < 8. (c) Hence or otherwise, for x ∈ ℝ, determine the range of values of x for which 1 < h(x) < 25 and represent your answer on a number line.
Think first: Notice first that h(x) = (x − 3)² — writing it that way turns every inequality into a simple square-root step.

contentBlocks.value: f(x) = x − 3, f²(x) = x − 6, f³(x) = x − 9, so each application subtracts a further 3

solutionSteps.instruction: Form gf(x) and compare with h.
Solve h(x) > 1 using the square form.

contentBlocks.value: Take the overlap of (x < 2 or x > 4) with -2 < x < 8

strategyBlocks.value: Track the repeated subtraction to get f⁴, compose g with f to recognise h as a perfect square, then solve each inequality using (x − 3)² and combine the two solution sets.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a)(i) f⁴(x) = x − 12 and f⁴(3) = -9  (a)(ii) gf(x) = (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9 = h(x)  (b)(i) x < 2 or x > 4  (b)(ii) (x − 3)² < 25 gives -5 < x − 3 < 5, hence -2 < x < 8  (c) -2 < x < 2 or 4 < x < 8, drawn on a number line as two open intervals with open circles at -2, 2, 4 and 8.

whyThisWorks.value: Because h(x) is the perfect square (x − 3)², its value depends only on how far x is from 3. So h(x) < 25 means x is within 5 of 3, and h(x) > 1 means x is more than 1 away from 3 — the first gives a single interval, the second gives two. Combining them leaves the points more than 1 but less than 5 away from 3, which is exactly the pair of intervals in the answer.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking only the positive root of (x − 3)² > 1 and losing the branch x < 2.
